scenario: Relevant cases are false negatives and receive lower/no review priority.
affected: People represented by cases that need attention; synthetic here, potentially serious if transferred to real services.
control: Do not use for real cases; retain manual no-score review; examine recall per group; suspend if recall gate fails; document reviewer overrides.
owner: Academic owner (risk assessment); institutional service owner unassigned.

scenario: Unequal error rates between protected groups may systematically disadvantage one group.
affected: People in groups with lower recall or higher FPR; communities affected by unequal attention.
control: Predefine subgroup gates; inspect recall and FPR by group; independent review before any change; halt if gates fail. Passing gates is not proof of fairness.
owner: Academic owner (risk assessment); institutional fairness owner unassigned.

scenario: Small intersectional cells make estimates unstable and can hide severe harms.
control: Report cell counts and uncertainty; do not infer safety from tiny cells; obtain adequate representative data and independent evaluation before real use.
owner: Academic owner (risk assessment); independent evaluator unassigned.

scenario: False positives consume reviewer capacity and may prompt unnecessary scrutiny.
affected: People whose cases are unnecessarily prioritized; operators bearing added workload.
control: Human review before any action; monitor FPR and workload; no adverse action from score; stop if review capacity or FPR tolerance is exceeded.
owner: Academic owner (risk assessment); operational reviewer owner unassigned.

scenario: Operator over-reliance on the score may turn a review aid into a de facto automated decision.
affected: People whose cases are reviewed; operators accountable for outcomes.
control: Label output as advisory; train reviewers; require independent human reasoning and override; audit decision logs and prohibit automatic intervention or eligibility decisions.
owner: Academic owner for exercise; operational service owner unassigned.

scenario: Model may be reused outside the stated synthetic purpose, including for real populations or high-impact decisions.
affected: People and communities subject to unauthorized profiling, intervention, or allocation decisions.
control: Restrict access and scope; prohibit real-person use; require documented purpose, legal approval, stakeholder assessment, and new gates before any proposed change; suspend on scope breach.
owner: Academic owner for exercise; institutional governance owner unassigned.

scenario: Data drift or pipeline/model changes may invalidate the measured performance and fairness results.
affected: People represented in future data; reviewers relying on stale metrics.
control: Version data, code, model, and gates; rerun temporal and subgroup evaluation on material changes; monitor approved indicators and rollback to manual review on failure.
owner: Academic owner for exercise; MLOps/monitoring owner unassigned.

scenario: Future ingestion of personal or directly identifying data could violate privacy expectations or legal requirements.
affected: Data subjects and communities; data stewards and institution.
control: Keep exercise data synthetic; enforce schema prohibition on direct identifiers; minimize data; require privacy/legal assessment and approved safeguards before any real-data processing.
owner: Academic owner for this exercise; institutional privacy officer unassigned.
